title: ECON 301 — Week 6: Heteroskedasticity
summary: Lecture notes covering the relaxation of the homoskedasticity assumption, its consequences for OLS inference, heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, tests for heteroskedasticity, and weighted least squares.

concepts.name: Heteroskedasticity
concepts.summary: Heteroskedasticity occurs when the conditional variance of the error term depends on the regressors, meaning Var(uᵢ | xᵢ) is not constant.

concepts.name: Robust standard errors
concepts.summary: Heteroskedasticity-robust variance estimators, such as White standard errors, allow for valid hypothesis testing in large samples even when error variance is non-constant.

concepts.name: Breusch–Pagan test
concepts.summary: The Breusch–Pagan test regresses squared OLS residuals on all regressors to test the null hypothesis of homoskedasticity against general heteroskedasticity.

concepts.name: White test
concepts.summary: The White test evaluates whether squared residuals are related to the regressors, their squares, and cross-products to detect broader forms of heteroskedasticity.

concepts.name: Weighted least squares
concepts.summary: Weighted least squares (WLS) is a transformation method used to restore efficiency when the functional form of heteroskedasticity is known or estimated.
